name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +16 partisan lean
Incumbent Joaquin Castro running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger raised under $50,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 98%
model.rationale: Castro is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 16 points, while his opponent has raised only about $49,000 and draws no outside spending. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at a wide margin.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention on the Republican side or an unexpected Castro scandal would be the main ways this becomes competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that voted Democratic by a wide margin in recent cycles. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised more than ten times what Republican Edgardo Rafael Baez has collected, and he holds a substantial cash-on-hand lead. No outside groups are active in the race, and no expert rating services list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Castro roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's partisan lean and the challenger's minimal campaign resources. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which all point the same direction. The seat is expected to remain safely in Democratic hands.
